role.altitude: The biomass plant manager keeps leading safety, judging deviations, deciding follow-up and supervising operations and maintenance crews; collecting emission figures, reading paper round sheets, building KPI and compliance tables and typing hours shrink.
skills_to_grow: Setting and reviewing alarm limits and the requirements register
role.ambitious_version: A manager who reads one morning page with every deviation flagged and spends the rest of the day on the plant.

tasks.short: Set the yearly safety plan, lead safety meetings and walks, have incidents reported, review and investigate them, track safety actions and training and report safety figures, to manage safety programs at the power generation facility.

steps.what: Biomass plant manager sets the yearly safety program from the risk inventory and incident trends
Biomass plant manager leads safety meetings and safety walks at the power generation facility
Employees and contractors report incidents and near misses: on a paper form today, on a phone form with photo and location after the change
Biomass plant manager gathers incident and near-miss reports with their photos and locations
Biomass plant manager reviews incident and near-miss reports and leads investigations

Biomass plant manager writes safety actions with owner and due date and follows up overdue ones and expiring training: in spreadsheets today, in the action register and training matrix after the change
Biomass plant manager checks the final actions: what each must fix, the finding it answers, owner and due date
Biomass plant manager assigns the checked actions to their owners in the register
Action owners update and close their own actions in the register
Biomass plant manager prepares the monthly safety figures with short comments: counted by hand today, read from the safety dashboard after the change
Biomass plant manager checks the final monthly figures and comments against the incidents and actions behind them
Biomass plant manager sends the checked safety figures to the plant director

tasks.design: Employees and contractors report incidents and near misses on a phone form in the safety system, with photo and location, instead of a paper form. The manager writes each action with owner and due date, checks it and assigns it in the register, which reminds owners; owners update their own actions (s6d), and the training matrix from HR records shows expiring safety training. A safety dashboard counts incidents, overdue actions and training status; the manager checks the monthly figures and sends them to the director. Setting the program, safety walks and investigations stay with the manager.

approvals.approved_version: The safety actions with what each must fix, the finding it answers, owner and due date exactly as checked by the manager in s6b, assigned once to the named owners in the action register; any change needs a new check.
The month's safety figures and comments exactly as checked by the manager in s7b, sent once to the plant director; any change needs a new check.

tasks.previous_blocker: Reports came on paper and actions were tracked in spreadsheets.
tasks.enabler_now: Mobile incident forms, action registers and training matrices in safety systems.
tasks.still_hard: Getting near misses reported at all.
tasks.human_edge: Earning the trust that makes people report their own mistakes.
tasks.altitude: Less administration around safety; leadership stays in person.

reach.learn: Whether a phone form raises near-miss reporting.

evidence.claim: Safety systems with mobile forms, action tracking and dashboards are standard products.
Incident and training records per person can monitor staff and need works council consent.

assumptions: Boundary: running the safety program; designing technical safety systems is outside.

Input contract for s6: actions written by the manager from investigation findings and closed by their owners (s6d, share 1); training dates kept by HR. s6 keeps 65 because writing actions stays; keeping spreadsheets and chasing drop.
Input contract for s7: incident reports entered by employees and contractors on the phone form (s3) with about the effort of the paper form, and the action register.
Walks, meetings and investigations keep their full or nearly full time; reporters' time is outside the manager's savings.
research_questions: Does near-miss reporting rise after the phone form?

incremental.description: Biomass plant manager keeps form categories and dashboard definitions current.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: contractors keep using paper forms, so s4 keeps 60, and many actions are still followed up by hand, so s6 keeps 80 (12.0); high: reports come through the phone form and owners close their own actions as designed (15.2).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Collect emission measurements, review biomass operations performance specifications against permit and subsidy requirements, check fuel sustainability documents, judge deviations, prepare the compliance report, have it approved and submit it.

steps.what: Biomass plant manager collects emission measurements and averages from the stack monitors and lab reports
Biomass plant manager reviews operations performance specifications for efficiency, emissions and fuel quality against the regulatory requirements
Fuel suppliers send sustainability certificates and declarations with their deliveries: by e-mail today, uploaded in the supplier portal after the change
Biomass plant manager checks the fuel sustainability documents against deliveries
Biomass plant manager judges deviations and decides measures
Biomass plant manager prepares the compliance report with tables and explanations
Plant director checks the final compliance report, its figures, explanations and measures, and signs it
Biomass plant manager submits the signed report on the authority's portal

approvals.approved_version: The compliance report with tables, explanations and measures exactly as checked and signed by the plant director in s7, submitted once on the authority's portal for this reporting period; any change needs a new check and signature.

tasks.design: The continuous emission monitors compute validated averages per period against the permit limits and export them, so the manager no longer copies them from the monitor screens. Permit and subsidy limits sit in a requirements register, and fixed comparisons show which values are inside or outside each limit. Fuel suppliers upload sustainability certificates per delivery in a supplier portal, matched to the weighbridge records. A report template fills the tables from the monitors and the register; the manager writes the explanations, the director signs, and the manager submits the signed version on the authority's portal. No model judges compliance.
tasks.previous_blocker: Emission figures, limits and fuel documents lived in separate screens, PDFs and mails.
tasks.enabler_now: Emission monitoring software that exports validated averages, and supplier portals for certificates.
tasks.still_hard: Explaining an exceedance and what the plant did about it.
tasks.human_edge: Knowing which deviation the authority will treat as serious.
tasks.altitude: Less compiling; compliance judgement and sign-off stay with people.

reach.task: Keep permits and subsidy conditions current
reach.learn: Whether the requirements register shows conditions nobody checks.

evidence.claim: Continuous emission monitoring systems compute validated averages and can export them.
AI used as a safety component in heat or electricity supply is an AI Act high-risk use; the design uses fixed comparisons only.

assumptions: Boundary: from measurements to the submitted compliance report; carrying out measures is outside.

Input contract for s1: validated period averages exported by the continuous emission monitors for continuously measured substances; periodic stack tests come as lab reports and are typed (about a third of values); s1 is priced at that share.
Input contract for s2: the requirements register with permit and subsidy limits, built and kept by the environmental coordinator.
Input contract for s4: certificates uploaded by fuel suppliers per delivery (s3) with about the effort of mailing them; weighbridge records from the fuel yard.
Judging deviations, signing and submitting keep their full time; director and supplier time are outside the manager's savings.
s6 keeps 70: the template fills the tables, but the explanations of deviations and measures are the manager's own writing.
unknowns: Reporting frequency required by the permit and subsidy.
research_questions: Do report corrections asked by the authority fall?

already_counted.description: Biomass plant manager checks monitor exports for invalid periods before use.

incremental.description: Environmental coordinator keeps the requirements register current when permits or subsidy rules change.
Biomass plant manager keeps the report template current.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: more values come from periodic stack tests typed from lab reports, so s1 keeps 60, and the tables need much rework, so s6 keeps 90 (23.5); high: monitor exports and the report template used as designed (31.5).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Have rounds recorded, review logs, datasheets or reports to ensure adequate production levels and safe production environments, identify abnormalities with power production equipment or processes, read maintenance reports and decide follow-up.

steps.what: Operators record actual readings on their plant rounds: on paper round sheets today, on a handheld app after the change
Biomass plant manager reviews shift logs and round sheets
Biomass plant manager reviews production reports to ensure adequate production levels: electricity, heat, fuel use and availability
Biomass plant manager reviews equipment datasheets and trends to identify abnormalities in boiler, flue gas and turbine
Biomass plant manager decides follow-up: operator instructions, load changes or work orders, and writes the work orders
Biomass plant manager checks each final work order: equipment, fault seen, readings behind it and urgency
Biomass plant manager submits the checked work orders to maintenance
Biomass plant manager reads maintenance and inspection reports

approvals.approved_version: Each work order with equipment, fault seen, readings and urgency exactly as checked by the manager in s5b, submitted once to the maintenance queue; any change needs a new check.

tasks.design: Operators record round readings on a handheld app that flags values outside fixed limits when they are entered, and shift logs are electronic, so the manager reads one list of flagged readings and log entries. A daily production page shows electricity and heat delivered, fuel use and availability from the meters and the control system historian. Trend pages with fixed limits per tag show abnormal boiler, flue gas and turbine values. Deciding follow-up and reading maintenance reports stay with the manager. No learning model touches the control system or any safety function.
tasks.previous_blocker: Readings were on paper round sheets and production figures were built in spreadsheets each morning.
tasks.enabler_now: Handheld round apps, historian dashboards and meter data.
tasks.still_hard: Slow drifts that stay inside the limits.
tasks.human_edge: Hearing that the boiler sounds different.
tasks.altitude: Less reading and compiling; judgement on abnormalities stays with the manager.

reach.learn: Whether flagged readings at entry make operators act sooner.

evidence.claim: Handheld round apps check readings against limits at entry; historians feed production dashboards.
AI used as a safety component in heat or electricity supply is an AI Act high-risk use; the design uses fixed limits only.

assumptions: Boundary: reviewing logs and data and deciding follow-up; doing the maintenance is outside.

Input contract for s2: actual readings entered by operators on the handheld during rounds (s1) with about the effort of the paper sheet; limits per reading set by the manager with the process engineer.
Input contract for s3: electricity and heat meters and fuel weighbridge data, plus the control system historian.
Input contract for s4: historian tags with fixed limits; drifts inside limits are found by the manager as today.

Follow-up decisions, writing and checking work orders, and maintenance reports keep their full time; operator time is outside the manager's savings. s3 keeps 50: the manager still reads the daily page; gathering meter and fuel figures from separate sources drops.
unknowns: Whether the historian is reachable outside the control room.

already_counted.description: Biomass plant manager checks flagged readings that turn out to be entry errors.

incremental.description: Biomass plant manager reviews tag limits with the process engineer each quarter.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: half of rounds stay on paper, so s2 keeps 80, and some meters are not linked, so s3 keeps 70 (17.1); high: handheld rounds and the daily production page used as designed (26.6).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Hold the daily meeting, supervise operations or maintenance employees in the production of power from biomass, plan rosters and on-call, approve clocked hours and have them passed to payroll, and coach staff.

steps.what: Employees clock in and out at the plant
Biomass plant manager holds the daily meeting with shift leaders and the maintenance lead
Biomass plant manager supervises operations and maintenance employees on the plant: fuel yard, boiler and turbine
Biomass plant manager plans shift and maintenance rosters including on-call
Biomass plant manager compares clocked hours and overtime with the roster and fixes missed clockings: by hand today, from the HCM's list of differences after the change
Biomass plant manager checks and approves the period's hours and overtime per employee against the roster and known absences
Biomass plant manager releases the approved hours to payroll: by mailed spreadsheet today, by one release through the HCM's payroll link after the change
Biomass plant manager coaches staff and holds performance talks

approvals.approved_version: The period's hours and overtime per employee exactly as checked by the manager in s5b, released once to the payroll office through the HCM's payroll link for this pay period; any later correction needs a new check and release.

tasks.design: Employees clock in and out with a badge at the gate, and the {HCM} compares clocked hours with the roster so the manager approves only the differences and overtime. Approved hours go to payroll through the HCM's payroll link instead of a mailed spreadsheet. Rosters and on-call are planned in the same app with minimum crew rules per shift. The daily meeting, supervision on the plant and coaching stay with the manager.
tasks.previous_blocker: Hours came from paper lists and went to payroll in a spreadsheet.
tasks.enabler_now: Badge clocks and HR apps that link rosters, hours and payroll.
tasks.still_hard: Covering an outage week with a small crew.
tasks.human_edge: Keeping an on-call crew willing to come out at night.
tasks.altitude: Less hours administration; supervision stays in person.

reach.learn: Whether linked hours cut pay corrections.

evidence.claim: Time clocks and roster data in HR systems can monitor presence and need works council consent.
HR systems compare clocked hours with rosters and send approved hours to payroll.

assumptions: Boundary: day-to-day supervision and hours; hiring and pay rates are outside.
Input contract for s5: actual start and end times from badge clocks at the gate (s1); missed clockings are fixed by the manager.

Input contract for s6: the HCM's payroll link, set up by HR; s6 keeps 10 for the release itself. s4 keeps 85: crew minimums are checked by the app, but planning rosters and on-call stays with the manager.
Meetings, supervision and coaching keep their full time; employee time is outside the manager's savings.
unknowns: Whether the plant has badge clocks.

already_counted.description: Biomass plant manager approves differences between clocked hours and roster.

incremental.description: Biomass plant manager keeps crew minimums current in the roster app.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: missed clockings are frequent, so s5 keeps 80, and rosters stay in the spreadsheet, so s4 keeps 100 (3.7); high: badge clocking and the roster app used as designed (7.8).
